blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

Key security observation confirmed: `globalThis.__loaderFileRead` remains defined for the entire lifetime of the runtime — any evaluated script (agent scripts, user job JS actions, LLM-generated scripts) can call it directly to read ANY file the process can read (e.g. `~/.dmtools/dmtools.env` with integration credentials, `/etc/passwd`, CI tokens in env files, SSH keys). var __loaderRead = globalThis.__loaderFileRead;
delete globalThis.__loaderFileRead;
```

So the capture must happen INSIDE the require bootstrap: at bootstrap eval time (inside installRequireLoader), capture `var loaderRead = globalThis.__loaderFileRead; delete globalThis.__loaderFileRead;` then use `loaderRead(resolvedPath)`. But installRequireLoader (line 138) runs BEFORE registerOn (line 154) — so at require-prelude eval time, `globalThis.__loaderFileRead` doesn't exist yet! So require must capture the function reference when the prelude INSTALLS... it can't (registered later).

Cleanest: flip the order in engine_factory (registerOn before installRequireLoader), then in the require bootstrap IIFE: `var loaderFileRead = globalThis.__loaderFileRead; delete globalThis.__loaderFileRead;` and call `loaderFileRead(resolvedPath)` inside readModuleCode. Alternatively make the property non-configurable but hidden? Can't hide from globalThis lookup — QuickJS globals are accessible. Could use a Symbol key? `globalThis[Symbol.for('__loaderFileRead')]` — agents could do the same. Closure capture + delete is the way.

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows).
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file carries
# only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository event
# triggers, the per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
#   issue assigned/labeled → factory guard → dev/review/rework leg
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual) → leg pinned by input
#
# Secrets (explicit mapping): SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required by the factory),
# Vars: FA_VERSION_MACHINE || FA_VERSION || latest, DMTOOLS_VERSION,
# ZAI_CODE_KEY, KIMI_REVIEW_KEY (optional provider keys).
# MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS.

name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && '🔧 rework' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  issues:
    # assigned only — labeled REMOVED (2026-10-01): every label echo (the dev
    # leg's own status:In Development, SM backfills) spawned a workflow run
    # that queued BEHIND the concurrency group for the whole leg duration
    # (live: gh-317/gh-318 twins, 20:01→20:03); the in-run dedupe gate cannot
    # act — workflow-level concurrency holds the whole run pending before any
    # job (incl. dedupe) starts. The awf guard skips status echoes at
    # evaluation, so no double EXECUTION — but the queue clutter was real.
    # Leg dispatching is dispatch-only: the SM dispatches review/rework
    # (workflow_dispatch, inputs.leg), the manual rework override (#544) is a
    # dispatch with leg=rework instead of the agent:rework label.
    types: [assigned]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string

Let me think hard about whether it's truly BLOCKING given the PR's intent and Java parity.

The threat model, carefully:
1. gh-365 built a deliberate, tested security boundary: agent-visible `file_read` (and the whole `file_*` family) is contained to job base/git root/tmpdir + configured allowlist. Its doc: "so the two cannot drift apart on a security-flavored behavior again". Tests assert the blocking ("Path traversal attempt blocked").
2. This PR intentionally exempts the require() loader path from that boundary (Java parity, justified: pack modules must load). The module path is host-resolved from `require()` args — and `require` is itself a global callable by any agent script with ANY absolute path. So even before considering `__loaderFileRead`, agent JS could do `require('/etc/some.js')` and (if it parses as JS) execute/inspect it — same as Java. That's the accepted-parity surface.
3. The additional exposure the PR creates beyond Java parity: `globalThis.__loaderFileRead` — a raw arbitrary-file-read function returning content as a string to ANY script, with no JS-parse requirement. E.g. `__loaderFileRead('/home/ubuntu/.dmtools/dmtools.env')` returns the credentials file content (env files with API tokens for Jira/GitHub/etc.). Java has no equivalent JS-callable primitive (loadJavaScriptCode is internal to loadModule; the only JS surface is require, which demands parseable JS and doesn't return source). So the Dart port hands untrusted scripts strictly more power than the Java spec does, and it defeats the gh-365 boundary by a one-liner.
4. Who runs agent scripts? dmtools executes job scripts from packs (semi-trusted, first-party-ish) AND job-provided JS actions (user/LLM-authored). The gh-365/367 work exists precisely because the project treats script-reachable file IO as security-flavored. A prompt-injected or malicious script could silently exfiltrate `~/.dmtools/dmtools.env`, SSH keys, CI tokens — the containment's whole point.

So: the raw global is a real security regression, cheap to fix (capture-into-closure + delete the global, e.g. inside installRequireLoader's bootstrap since it runs before registerOn? No — order is installRequireLoader BEFORE registerOn, so at prelude-eval time the global doesn't exist yet. Fixes: (a) reorder in wireEngine (move ToolBridge.registerOn before installRequireLoader — but the engine_factory doc says host functions must be LAST so direct file_read wins over generated wrapper; the ordering constraint is about wrappers vs file_read, and installRequireLoader before host functions is fine to move? The comment says "host functions last, so the direct file_read global wins over the generated wrapper" — moving registerOn earlier keeps it after wrappers, satisfying that constraint; then the require prelude can capture & delete). Or (b) the hostFunctionsBootstrap itself defines `__loaderFileRead`, and the require loader... also runs before. Hmm (c): registerOn could eval a tiny cleanup AFTER wiring: in wireEngine after registerOn, eval `delete globalThis.__loaderFileRead;`? Then require breaks (global lookup at call time). So the require prelude must capture the reference. The cleanest minimal fix: registerOn (which evals hostFunctionsBootstrap) can, immediately after, capture and remove: `runtime.eval('globalThis.__requireFileRead = globalThis.__loaderFileRead; delete globalThis.__loaderFileRead;')` — and change require_loader to call `__requireFileRead`? Same leak (renamed global). The capture must live INSIDE a closure that require uses. blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

Now let me look at engine_factory.dart to understand the setup order (installRequireLoader at line 138, registerOn at line 154 — installRequireLoader runs BEFORE registerOn). Interesting: installRequireLoader evals the require prelude which references `__loaderFileRead` only at require() call time. registerOn (line 154) registers the host function and evals hostFunctionsBootstrap that defines `globalThis.__loaderFileRead`. Both happen before any script eval, so it works.

Key security observation confirmed: `globalThis.__loaderFileRead` remains defined for the entire lifetime of the runtime — any evaluated script (agent scripts, user job JS actions, LLM-generated scripts) can call it directly to read ANY file the process can read (e.g. `~/.dmtools/dmtools.env` with integration credentials, `/etc/passwd`, CI tokens in env files, SSH keys). This bypasses the gh-365/gh-367 containment that was explicitly built as a security boundary ("Path traversal attempt blocked", security-flavored behavior, gh-365 rework review threads). The comment "Never referenced by agent code" describes hope, not a boundary.

Fix is cheap: after installRequireLoader's prelude captures `__loaderFileRead` into its closure, remove the global. E.g. in engine_factory or in the require bootstrap:

```js
var __loaderRead = globalThis.__loaderFileRead;
delete globalThis.__loaderFileRead;
```

inside the require loader IIFE, OR in engine_factory after both installs: eval a tiny snippet `delete globalThis.__loaderFileRead;`. But careful: `require` is only invoked at script runtime, and the prelude closure captures `__loaderFileRead` by global lookup at call time... The require bootstrap references `__loaderFileRead(resolvedPath)` — global lookup at call time. If we delete the global, require breaks. So the capture must happen INSIDE the require bootstrap: at bootstrap eval time (inside installRequireLoader), capture `var loaderRead = globalThis.__loaderFileRead; delete globalThis.__loaderFileRead;` then use `loaderRead(resolvedPath)`. But installRequireLoader (line 138) runs BEFORE registerOn (line 154) — so at require-prelude eval time, `globalThis.__loaderFileRead` doesn't exist yet! Order: engine_factory 138 installRequireLoader → 154 ToolBridge.registerOn. So capture-at-install wouldn't work unless the order flips or the wrapper stores it elsewhere.

Alternative: registerOn's bootstrap could define `__loaderFileRead` as non-enumerable/writable:false? QuickJS supports Object.defineProperty. Or define it as a getter that... simplest: after both installs, engine_factory evals `delete globalThis.__loaderFileRead;` — but then require at script runtime does global lookup → undefined → content undefined → 'JavaScript file not found'. So require must capture the function reference when the prelude INSTALLS... it can't (registered later).

Cleanest: flip the order in engine_factory (registerOn before installRequireLoader), then in the require bootstrap IIFE: `var loaderFileRead = globalThis.__loaderFileRead; delete globalThis.__loaderFileRead;` and call `loaderFileRead(resolvedPath)` inside readModuleCode. That removes the global from agent reach while require keeps a closure-captured reference. That's a concrete, workable fix suggestion.

Alternatively make the property non-configurable but hidden? Can't hide from globalThis lookup — QuickJS globals are accessible. Could use a Symbol key? `globalThis[Symbol.for('__loaderFileRead')]` — agents could do the same. Closure capture + delete is the way.

Also `require()` itself: with the global deleted, require is still an uncontained read primitive for agent scripts (Java parity though — the ticket explicitly wants that; the review can note it as accepted-by-design, SUGGESTION/observation, not blocking, since Java parity is the stated spec and the live failure demanded it. The file must contain parseable JS for require to return exports; content doesn't leak directly... well, actually a module CAN leak its own content: configLoader.js is not attacker-controlled. But require of arbitrary existing files under agent control — agent scripts could first file_write a JS file inside the sandbox and then require it — that's just eval of their own content, already possible via eval(). require of host files: only leaks content if the content is valid JS that assigns exports... e.g., JSON files! `require('/home/user/secret.json')` — JSON is valid JS expression? `{"a": 1}` — as JS statement `{ "a": 1 }` is a block with a string-labeled... no, `"a": 1` is invalid as a labeled statement (labels must be identifiers). So JSON files fail to parse. What about .js config files elsewhere? The exfiltration surface via require alone is narrow; via the leaked `__loaderFileRead` global it's everything. So the global deletion fix restores most of the boundary.

Let me think hard about whether it's truly BLOCKING given the PR's intent and Java parity.

The threat model, carefully:
1. gh-365 built a deliberate, tested security boundary: agent-visible `file_read` (and the whole `file_*` family) is contained to job base/git root/tmpdir + configured allowlist. Its doc: "so the two cannot drift apart on a security-flavored behavior again". Tests assert the blocking ("Path traversal attempt blocked").
2. This PR intentionally exempts the require() loader path from that boundary (Java parity, justified: pack modules must load). The module path is host-resolved from `require()` args — and `require` is itself a global callable by any agent script with ANY absolute path. So even before considering `__loaderFileRead`, agent JS could do `require('/etc/some.js')` and (if it parses as JS) execute/inspect it — same as Java. That's the accepted-parity surface.
3. The additional exposure the PR creates beyond Java parity: `globalThis.__loaderFileRead` — a raw arbitrary-file-read function returning content as a string to ANY script, with no JS-parse requirement. E.g. `__loaderFileRead('/home/ubuntu/.dmtools/dmtools.env')` returns the credentials file content (env files with API tokens for Jira/GitHub/etc.). Java has no equivalent JS-callable primitive (loadJavaScriptCode is internal to loadModule; the only JS surface is require, which demands parseable JS and doesn't return source). So the Dart port hands untrusted scripts strictly more power than the Java spec does, and it defeats the gh-365 boundary by a one-liner.
4. Who runs agent scripts? dmtools executes job scripts from packs (semi-trusted, first-party-ish) AND job-provided JS actions (user/LLM-authored). The gh-365/367 work exists precisely because the project treats script-reachable file IO as security-flavored. A prompt-injected or malicious script could silently exfiltrate `~/.dmtools/dmtools.env`, SSH keys, CI tokens — the containment's whole point.

So: the raw global is a real security regression, cheap to fix (capture-into-closure + delete the global, e.g. inside installRequireLoader's bootstrap since it runs before registerOn? No — order is installRequireLoader BEFORE registerOn, so at prelude-eval time the global doesn't exist yet. Fixes: (a) reorder in wireEngine (move ToolBridge.registerOn before installRequireLoader — but the engine_factory doc says host functions must be LAST so direct file_read wins over generated wrapper; the ordering constraint is about wrappers vs file_read, and installRequireLoader before host functions is fine to move? The comment says "host functions last, so the direct file_read global wins over the generated wrapper" — moving registerOn earlier keeps it after wrappers, satisfying that constraint; then the require prelude can capture & delete). Or (b) the hostFunctionsBootstrap itself defines `__loaderFileRead`, and the require loader... also runs before. Hmm (c): registerOn could eval a tiny cleanup AFTER wiring: in wireEngine after registerOn, eval `delete globalThis.__loaderFileRead;`? Then require breaks (global lookup at call time). So the require prelude must capture the reference. The cleanest minimal fix: registerOn (which evals hostFunctionsBootstrap) can, immediately after, capture and remove: `runtime.eval('globalThis.__requireFileRead = globalThis.__loaderFileRead; delete globalThis.__loaderFileRead;')` — and change require_loader to call `__requireFileRead`? Same leak (renamed global). The capture must live INSIDE a closure that require uses. So: in `installRequireLoader`, wrap: eval a snippet that at install time reads `globalThis.__loaderFileRead` into the loader closure... but install runs before registerOn. OK so real fix = swap the two wiring steps in wireEngine (registerOn before installRequireLoader), then inside the require bootstrap IIFE: `var loaderRead = globalThis.__loaderFileRead; delete globalThis.__loaderFileRead;` and use `loaderRead(...)` in readModuleCode. That preserves the "host functions last" constraint partially... wait the constraint is host functions AFTER tool wrappers (wrappers are eval'd before registerOn already; installRequireLoader sits between wrappers and host functions but the constraint is only wrapper-vs-file_read precedence). Swapping installRequireLoader and ToolBridge.registerOn keeps wrappers before both. The require prelude captures the function; require works; agent scripts can no longer r…

Actually wait — maybe the single-arg marshaling is: argsJson = the RAW string WITHOUT quotes (not JSON). Then jsonDecode(raw path) throws FormatException → parsed=null → return 'null'. That matches the observed null! The doc in loader_read_host says "a single string argument as the JSON string itself" — but empirically for this runtime version, a single string arg seems to arrive WITHOUT JSON quoting (or as something non-JSON). Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||

      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && '🔧 rework' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{

The threat model, carefully:
1. gh-365 built a deliberate, tested security boundary: agent-visible `file_read` (and the whole `file_*` family) is contained to job base/git root/tmpdir + configured allowlist. Its doc: "so the two cannot drift apart on a security-flavored behavior again". Tests assert the blocking ("Path traversal attempt blocked").
2. This PR intentionally exempts the require() loader path from that boundary (Java parity, justified: pack modules must load). The module path is host-resolved from `require()` args — and `require` is itself a global callable by any agent script with ANY absolute path. So even before considering `__loaderFileRead`, agent JS could do `require('/etc/some.js')` and (if it parses as JS) execute/inspect it — same as Java. That's the accepted-parity surface.
3. The additional exposure the PR creates beyond Java parity: `globalThis.__loaderFileRead` — a raw arbitrary-file-read function returning content as a string to ANY script, with no JS-parse requirement. E.g. `__loaderFileRead('/home/ubuntu/.dmtools/dmtools.env')` returns the credentials file content (env files with API tokens for Jira/GitHub/etc.). Java has no equivalent JS-callable primitive (loadJavaScriptCode is internal to loadModule; the only JS surface is require, which demands parseable JS and doesn't return source). So the Dart port hands untrusted scripts strictly more power than the Java spec does, and it defeats the gh-365 boundary by a one-liner.
4. Who runs agent scripts? dmtools executes job scripts from packs (semi-trusted, first-party-ish) AND job-provided JS actions (user/LLM-authored). The gh-365/367 work exists precisely because the project treats script-reachable file IO as security-flavored. A prompt-injected or malicious script could silently exfiltrate `~/.dmtools/dmtools.env`, SSH keys, CI tokens — the containment's whole point.

So: the raw global is a real security regression, cheap to fix (capture-into-closure + delete the global, e.g. inside installRequireLoader's bootstrap since it runs before registerOn? No — order is installRequireLoader BEFORE registerOn, so at prelude-eval time the global doesn't exist yet. Fixes: (a) reorder in wireEngine (move ToolBridge.registerOn before installRequireLoader — but the engine_factory doc says host functions must be LAST so direct file_read wins over generated wrapper; the ordering constraint is about wrappers vs file_read, and installRequireLoader before host functions is fine to move? The comment says "host functions last, so the direct file_read global wins over the generated wrapper" — moving registerOn earlier keeps it after wrappers, satisfying that constraint; then the require prelude can capture & delete). Or (b) the hostFunctionsBootstrap itself defines `__loaderFileRead`, and the require loader... also runs before. Hmm (c): registerOn could eval a tiny cleanup AFTER wiring: in wireEngine after registerOn, eval `delete globalThis.__loaderFileRead;`? Then require breaks (global lookup at call time). So the require prelude must capture the reference. The cleanest minimal fix: registerOn (which evals hostFunctionsBootstrap) can, immediately after, capture and remove: `runtime.eval('globalThis.__requireFileRead = globalThis.__loaderFileRead; delete globalThis.__loaderFileRead;')` — and change require_loader to call `__requireFileRead`? Same leak (renamed global). The capture must live INSIDE a closure that require uses. So: in `installRequireLoader`, wrap: eval a snippet that at install time reads `globalThis.__loaderFileRead` into the loader closure... but install runs before registerOn. OK so real fix = swap the two wiring steps in wireEngine (registerOn before installRequireLoader), then inside the require bootstrap IIFE: `var loaderRead = globalThis.__loaderFileRead; delete globalThis.__loaderFileRead;` and use `loaderRead(...)` in readModuleCode. That preserves the "host functions last" constraint partially... wait the constraint is host functions AFTER tool wrappers (wrappers are eval'd before registerOn already; installRequireLoader sits between wrappers and host functions but the constraint is only wrapper-vs-file_read precedence). Swapping installRequireLoader and ToolBridge.registerOn keeps wrappers before both. The require prelude captures the function; require works; agent scripts can no longer r…

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Closes #369.

Live failure: SM manual tick on v0.1.41 (after the unpin) — every pack-internal require blocked as path traversal, tick exit 1. Interim DMTOOLS_VERSION=v0.1.39 pin stays until this releases (>v0.1.41), then unpin per the owner's rollout order (dart first, verify, then fa).

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

#
#   issue assigned/labeled → factory guard → dev/review/rework leg
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual) → leg pinned by input
#
# Secrets (explicit mapping): SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required by the factory),
# Vars: FA_VERSION_MACHINE || FA_VERSION || latest, DMTOOLS_VERSION,
# ZAI_CODE_KEY, KIMI_REVIEW_KEY (optional provider keys).

name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && '🔧 rework' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{

The threat model, carefully:
1. gh-365 built a deliberate, tested security boundary: agent-visible `file_read` (and the whole `file_*` family) is contained to job base/git root/tmpdir + configured allowlist. Its doc: "so the two cannot drift apart on a security-flavored behavior again". Tests assert the blocking ("Path traversal attempt blocked").
2. This PR intentionally exempts the require() loader path from that boundary (Java parity, justified: pack modules must load). The module path is host-resolved from `require()` args — and `require` is itself a global callable by any agent script with ANY absolute path. So even before considering `__loaderFileRead`, agent JS could do `require('/etc/some.js')` and (if it parses as JS) execute/inspect it — same as Java. That's the accepted-parity surface.
3. The additional exposure the PR creates beyond Java parity: `globalThis.__loaderFileRead` — a raw arbitrary-file-read function returning content as a string to ANY script, with no JS-parse requirement. E.g. `__loaderFileRead('/home/ubuntu/.dmtools/dmtools.env')` returns the credentials file content (env files with API tokens for Jira/GitHub/etc.). Java has no equivalent JS-callable primitive (loadJavaScriptCode is internal to loadModule; the only JS surface is require, which demands parseable JS and doesn't return source). So the Dart port hands untrusted scripts strictly more power than the Java spec does, and it defeats the gh-365 boundary by a one-liner.
4. Who runs agent scripts? dmtools executes job scripts from packs (semi-trusted, first-party-ish) AND job-provided JS actions (user/LLM-authored). The gh-365/367 work exists precisely because the project treats script-reachable file IO as security-flavored. A prompt-injected or malicious script could silently exfiltrate `~/.dmtools/dmtools.env`, SSH keys, CI tokens — the containment's whole point.

So: the raw global is a real security regression, cheap to fix (capture-into-closure + delete the global, e.g. inside installRequireLoader's bootstrap since it runs before registerOn? No — order is installRequireLoader BEFORE registerOn, so at prelude-eval time the global doesn't exist yet. Fixes: (a) reorder in wireEngine (move ToolBridge.registerOn before installRequireLoader — but the engine_factory doc says host functions must be LAST so direct file_read wins over generated wrapper; the ordering constraint is about wrappers vs file_read, and installRequireLoader before host functions is fine to move? The comment says "host functions last, so the direct file_read global wins over the generated wrapper" — moving registerOn earlier keeps it after wrappers, satisfying that constraint; then the require prelude can capture & delete). Or (b) the hostFunctionsBootstrap itself defines `__loaderFileRead`, and the require loader... also runs before. Hmm (c): registerOn could eval a tiny cleanup AFTER wiring: in wireEngine after registerOn, eval `delete globalThis.__loaderFileRead;`? Then require breaks (global lookup at call time). So the require prelude must capture the reference. The cleanest minimal fix: registerOn (which evals hostFunctionsBootstrap) can, immediately after, capture and remove: `runtime.eval('globalThis.__requireFileRead = globalThis.__loaderFileRead; delete globalThis.__loaderFileRead;')` — and change require_loader to call `__requireFileRead`? Same leak (renamed global). The capture must live INSIDE a closure that require uses. So: in `installRequireLoader`, wrap: eval a snippet that at install time reads `globalThis.__loaderFileRead` into the loader closure... but install runs before registerOn. OK so real fix = swap the two wiring steps in wireEngine (registerOn before installRequireLoader), then inside the require bootstrap IIFE: `var loaderRead = globalThis.__loaderFileRead; delete globalThis.__loaderFileRead;` and use `loaderRead(...)` in readModuleCode. That preserves the "host functions last" constraint partially... wait the constraint is host functions AFTER tool wrappers (wrappers are eval'd before registerOn already; installRequireLoader sits between wrappers and host functions but the constraint is only wrapper-vs-file_read precedence). Swapping installRequireLoader and ToolBridge.registerOn keeps wrappers before both. The require prelude captures the function; require works; agent scripts can no longer r…

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

Both happen before any script eval, so it works.

Key security observation confirmed: `globalThis.__loaderFileRead` remains defined for the entire lifetime of the runtime — any evaluated script (agent scripts, user job JS actions, LLM-generated scripts) can call it directly to read ANY file the process can read (e.g. `~/.dmtools/dmtools.env` with integration credentials, `/etc/passwd`, CI tokens in env files, SSH keys). This bypasses the gh-365/gh-367 containment that was explicitly built as a security boundary ("Path traversal attempt blocked", security-flavored behavior, gh-365 rework review threads). The comment "Never referenced by agent code" describes hope, not a boundary.

Fix is cheap: after installRequireLoader's prelude captures `__loaderFileRead` into its closure, remove the global. E.g. in engine_factory or in the require bootstrap:

```js
var __loaderRead = globalThis.__loaderFileRead;
delete globalThis.__loaderFileRead;
```

inside the require loader IIFE, OR in engine_factory after both installs: eval a tiny snippet `delete globalThis.__loaderFileRead;`. But careful: `require` is only invoked at script runtime, and the prelude closure captures `__loaderFileRead` by global lookup at call time... The require bootstrap references `__loaderFileRead(resolvedPath)` — global lookup at call time. If we delete the global, require breaks. So the capture must happen INSIDE the require bootstrap: at bootstrap eval time (inside installRequireLoader), capture `var loaderRead = globalThis.__loaderFileRead; delete globalThis.__loaderFileRead;` then use `loaderRead(resolvedPath)`. But installRequireLoader (line 138) runs BEFORE registerOn (line 154) — so at require-prelude eval time, `globalThis.__loaderFileRead` doesn't exist yet! Order: engine_factory 138 installRequireLoader → 154 ToolBridge.registerOn. So capture-at-install wouldn't work unless the order flips or the wrapper stores it elsewhere.

Alternative: registerOn's bootstrap could define `__loaderFileRead` as non-enumerable/writable:false? QuickJS supports Object.defineProperty. Or define it as a getter that... simplest: after both installs, engine_factory evals `delete globalThis.__loaderFileRead;` — but then require at script runtime does global lookup → undefined → content undefined → 'JavaScript file not found'. So require must capture the function reference when the prelude INSTALLS... it can't (registered later).

Cleanest: flip the order in engine_factory (registerOn before installRequireLoader), then in the require bootstrap IIFE: `var loaderFileRead = globalThis.__loaderFileRead; delete globalThis.__loaderFileRead;` and call `loaderFileRead(resolvedPath)` inside readModuleCode. That removes the global from agent reach while require keeps a closure-captured reference. That's a concrete, workable fix suggestion.

Alternatively make the property non-configurable but hidden? Can't hide from globalThis lookup — QuickJS globals are accessible. Could use a Symbol key? `globalThis[Symbol.for('__loaderFileRead')]` — agents could do the same. Closure capture + delete is the way.

Also `require()` itself: with the global deleted, require is still an uncontained read primitive for agent scripts (Java parity though — the ticket explicitly wants that; the review can note it as accepted-by-design, SUGGESTION/observation, not blocking, since Java parity is the stated spec and the live failure demanded it. The file must contain parseable JS for require to return exports; content doesn't leak directly... well, actually a module CAN leak its own content: configLoader.js is not attacker-controlled. But require of arbitrary existing files under agent control — agent scripts could first file_write a JS file inside the sandbox and then require it — that's just eval of their own content, already possible via eval(). require of host files: only leaks content if the content is valid JS that assigns exports... e.g., JSON files! `require('/home/user/secret.json')` — JSON is valid JS expression? `{"a": 1}` — as JS statement `{ "a": 1 }` is a block with a string-labeled... no, `"a": 1` is invalid as a labeled statement (labels must be identifiers). So JSON files fail to parse. What about .js config files elsewhere? The exfiltration surface via require alone is narrow; via the leaked `__loaderFileRead` global it's everything. So the global deletion fix restores most of the boundary.

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows).

name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,

        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||

      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)

    # Leg dispatching is dispatch-only: the SM dispatches review/rework
    # (workflow_dispatch, inputs.leg), the manual rework override (#544) is a
    # dispatch with leg=rework instead of the agent:rework label.
    types: [assigned]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:

        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
